projects/skylabs/index.html.title: From aircraft sensors to a flight record
projects/skylabs/index.html.role: I developed the STM32 aircraft logger, ESP32 LoRa ground station and post-flight replay tools. I joined Skylabs in August 2025 and became Avionics & Payload Team Lead in May 2026.
projects/skylabs/index.html.constraint: Sensors update at different rates, the radio carries a smaller live subset, and the team still needs a useful record after landing.
projects/skylabs/index.html.decision: Keep the aircraft binary log separate from the live link. Record the received packets again on the ground, then use one data contract for synchronized replay.
projects/skylabs/index.html.test: The published F110211 flight contains 13,772 rows over 679.33 seconds. Its report records a 50.0 ms log interval, 13,402 log overruns and zero SD write errors.
projects/skylabs/index.html.limit: 40 Hz is the aircraft logger’s target. This flight does not demonstrate sustained 40 Hz logging; zero SD write errors does not mean every timing deadline was met.
projects/skylabs/index.html.disclosure: The recorded flight includes its exact GPS route.

hero.alt: Assembled blue Skylabs aircraft telemetry PCB with its sensors, microSD socket and radio

projects/tramtrace/index.html.title: The map is also the circuit board
projects/tramtrace/index.html.role: PCB design, embedded display logic and the vehicle-position service that feeds the board over Wi-Fi.
projects/tramtrace/index.html.constraint: Four light-rail lines, station labels, 116 RGB pixels and the controller circuitry share a 207.81 × 94.55 mm board.
projects/tramtrace/index.html.decision: Use the silkscreen as the map, an ESP32 for network and display logic, and level shifting between the controller and LED data. Five electrical chains carry the pixels.
projects/tramtrace/index.html.test: The build photographs show an assembled, illuminated display. The production-board explorer exposes the copper layers and plays a frame through the source-derived LED order.
projects/tramtrace/index.html.limit: The photographs establish the physical build. The data-frame explorer explains electrical order; it is not a measurement of live update latency or service uptime.

hero.alt: The built TramTrace board illuminated with Sydney and Parramatta light-rail routes

projects/metroboard/index.html.title: Live rail data, made physical
projects/metroboard/index.html.role: A custom Sydney rail-map PCB and a service that supplies TfNSW GTFS real-time vehicle positions to the Wi-Fi-connected board.
projects/metroboard/index.html.constraint: The display is a 300 × 305.7 mm PCB with 291 RGB pixels. Copper, solder mask and silkscreen must communicate the network without a separate screen or printed overlay.
projects/metroboard/index.html.decision: Make the PCB itself the interface, with LEDs positioned on the rail map. The same approach later informed TramTrace’s smaller, tighter light-rail layout.
projects/metroboard/index.html.test: The published photographs show the unlit PCB, controller edge and illuminated network. The assembly view makes the placement of the pixels and support circuitry inspectable.
projects/metroboard/index.html.limit: This is build and display evidence. No measured refresh latency, fleet-position accuracy or long-duration reliability result is published here.

hero.alt: The assembled Metroboard displaying illuminated Sydney rail routes in a dark room

projects/framework-dual-usb/index.html.title: A useful trade-off inside one bay
projects/framework-dual-usb/index.html.role: A custom two-port USB hub PCB packaged in the standard Framework expansion-card enclosure.
projects/framework-dual-usb/index.html.constraint: Three Type-C connectors, a hub, power switching, protection and their supporting parts must fit inside one laptop bay.
projects/framework-dual-usb/index.html.decision: Keep the design at USB 2.0 for small peripherals. A CH334F handles the hub, TPS2065 switches limit downstream power, and USBLC6-2SC6 parts provide connector-side ESD protection.
projects/framework-dual-usb/index.html.test: Photographs show the assembled PCB, both downstream ports and the card installed in a Framework laptop. The assembly viewer shows the board, enclosure and component arrangement.
projects/framework-dual-usb/index.html.limit: The published material establishes the build and installed fit. It does not include USB compliance, sustained throughput, ESD-test or power-limit measurements.

projects/skylabs/boards/telemetry/index..title: Keep missing data distinguishable
projects/skylabs/boards/telemetry/index..role: The STM32G474 aircraft PCB, sensor acquisition, binary logging and the aircraft side of the SX1262 link.
projects/skylabs/boards/telemetry/index..constraint: Acceleration, attitude, GNSS and other sensors have different update rates and failure modes. A sample also needs to say whether its inputs are present and valid.
projects/skylabs/boards/telemetry/index..decision: Store presence and validity with measurements and represent missing values as NaN. Batch eight records per SD transaction and sync once a second, with a 40 Hz logging target.
projects/skylabs/boards/telemetry/index..test: F110211 provides a replayable recorded flight. The report shows a 50.0 ms log interval, 13,402 overruns, zero SD write errors and zero IMU resets.
projects/skylabs/boards/telemetry/index..limit: That report separates storage and timing outcomes. It does not establish that the 40 Hz target was sustained, or explain the cause of the overruns.
projects/skylabs/boards/telemetry/index..disclosure: The recorded flight includes its exact GPS route.

projects/skylabs/boards/ground-station/i.title: A second record at the field
projects/skylabs/boards/ground-station/i.role: An ESP32-WROOM-32E ground-station PCB bringing together the SX1262 receiver, microSD storage, OLED connection and field controls.
projects/skylabs/boards/ground-station/i.constraint: The crew needs telemetry and logging controls without depending on a laptop, plus a separate record if the aircraft log becomes inaccessible.
projects/skylabs/boards/ground-station/i.decision: Store valid received packets locally as CSV or indexed, CRC-protected binary. Expose link and sensor status on the OLED, and provide a phone-ready Wi-Fi dashboard and pre-flight checklist.
projects/skylabs/boards/ground-station/i.test: The published build photographs show the receiver, antenna connection and microSD hardware. The documented workflow adds a rate-limited USB stream for another record on a laptop.
projects/skylabs/boards/ground-station/i.limit: A ground log contains the received live subset, not the full aircraft log. No packet-loss benchmark or damaged-record recovery test result is published here.

hero.alt: Assembled blue Skylabs ground-station PCB with LoRa module, microSD and USB-C

projects/rf-test-board/index.html.title: Turn a feedline problem into a test coupon
projects/rf-test-board/index.html.role: A two-layer RF comparison board, ordered without impedance control and measured with a vector network analyser.
projects/rf-test-board/index.html.constraint: Calculator geometry needed checking against the inexpensive 1.6 mm FR-4 process I was actually using.
projects/rf-test-board/index.html.decision: Place masked and unmasked coplanar traces, u.FL and SMA transitions, tuning sections and split-pi footprints on the same board. Print the stack-up and nominal widths on the reverse.
projects/rf-test-board/index.html.test: The case study documents VNA measurement and the physical comparison structures. The target is 50 Ω with 1 oz outer copper and a 0.2 mm gap to the surrounding copper.
projects/rf-test-board/index.html.limit: 50 Ω is a design target. Measured S-parameter plots and a numerical pass/fail result are not included in the public case study.

projects/lora-receiver/index.html.title: A range result, and a better RF question
projects/lora-receiver/index.html.role: A receiver PCB combining an ESP32 application controller, 915 MHz LoRa and a u-blox NEO-M9N GNSS receiver.
projects/lora-receiver/index.html.constraint: Putting radio and navigation on one board reduces external wiring, but makes the feedline layout part of the system design.
projects/lora-receiver/index.html.decision: Check the Rev A feedline with a VNA. Its mismatch from the 50 Ω target informed a dedicated RF test board for comparing geometries and transitions.
projects/lora-receiver/index.html.test: The published case records a link reaching at least one kilometre in testing, alongside the VNA investigation of the first-pass feedline.
projects/lora-receiver/index.html.limit: The distance is a reported test result. The page does not publish a complete range-test setup, packet-loss curve or measured impedance value.

projects/framework-expansion-card/index..title: Board thickness is an interface decision
projects/framework-expansion-card/index..role: An ESP32-S3-MINI-1 development board integrated into a Framework expansion bay, including USB serial, power and automatic boot/reset circuitry.
projects/framework-expansion-card/index..constraint: The laptop connection, module keep-out and component placement all have to fit the expansion-card outline.
projects/framework-expansion-card/index..decision: Use a 0.6 mm PCB to mate directly with the laptop’s USB-C connector. A CH340K and BC817 transistor pair support programming; the clear enclosure leaves the antenna end unobstructed.
projects/framework-expansion-card/index..test: The photographs show the latest black PCB assembled in its enclosure, circuit details and the earlier green revision.
projects/framework-expansion-card/index..limit: The public evidence covers revisions and physical assembly. It does not provide a measured radio comparison or connector-cycle reliability test.

projects/framework-raspberry-pi/index.ht.title: An RP2354B in the Framework outline
projects/framework-raspberry-pi/index.ht.role: A 26 × 30 mm microcontroller-board design for a Framework laptop expansion bay.
projects/framework-raspberry-pi/index.ht.constraint: The 0.8 mm PCB, straddle-mount USB-C plug, mounting points and tactile controls share the small expansion-card envelope.
projects/framework-raspberry-pi/index.ht.decision: Arrange the RP2354B, external flash, crystal and power circuit around the connector and reference-enclosure mounting points.
projects/framework-raspberry-pi/index.ht.test: The source-derived assembly makes the board layout and relationship to the reference enclosure inspectable.
projects/framework-raspberry-pi/index.ht.limit: This page presents design and CAD evidence. It does not establish a manufactured, electrically tested or installed card.
